checks.explanation: US home price growth decelerated sharply and prices declined in many markets through the following quarters as mortgage rates rose in 2022-2023.
Consumers faced significant financial strain from inflation and rising borrowing costs through the following months of 2022.
The US did see a technical GDP contraction in the first half of 2022, but no NBER-declared recession occurred within the following 1-2 years as the economy instead achieved a broad soft landing.

The Fed did begin quantitative tightening around mid-2022 at a pace ramping toward roughly $95 billion per month, broadly matching the prediction, though QT was scaled back and effectively ended in 2024 before the full $3 trillion runoff was achieved.
No stagflationary recession materialized; inflation declined through 2023-2024 while economic growth continued, achieving a soft landing instead.
US real GDP was negative in both Q1 and Q2 2022, technically meeting the common two-consecutive-quarter definition of recession.
Consumer credit card debt did rise to record levels with increasing delinquencies through 2022-2024, though it was not characterized as a full-blown credit-bubble crisis.
US residential real estate saw price declines in 2022-2023 but no systemic 2008-style collapse occurred.
US unemployment remained near multi-decade lows (around 3.5-3.7%) through 2022-2023 and did not begin rising meaningfully until 2024-2025.
The venture and growth-equity ecosystem did undergo a multi-year period of painful adjustment, including widespread layoffs, down rounds, and restructuring through 2022-2024.
Venture funding through the downturn broadly favored startups with strong growth and capital efficiency, while moderate-growth, high-burn companies struggled to raise capital.
Large traditional venture funds did slow their deployment pace significantly after the 2020-2021 boom, moving back toward multi-year deployment cycles through 2022-2024.
Crossover investors such as Tiger Global pulled back sharply from private tech investing after 2022 and remained far less active for an extended period.

Several VC-backed companies (OpenAI, SpaceX, Anthropic) grew to very large private valuations approaching or exceeding hundreds of billions of dollars by 2025, though a clean case of a new trillion-dollar company directly emerging from that specific 2022 dry-powder pool is not yet fully established.
VC capital did fund new company and job creation in the following years, though isolating this specific stimulative effect at the scale described is difficult to verify cleanly.
No acute consumer credit crisis materialized within the predicted 9-12 month window by mid-2023; credit stress built more gradually over subsequent years instead.
The S&P 500 continued falling well below 3,800, bottoming around 3,577 in October 2022, roughly 6% further than predicted, without an immediate Fed-put rescue at that level.
